references.text: The same chapter describes physical defects that disqualify priests from service, paralleling the requirements for unblemished sacrificial animals.
The immediate context establishes that sacrificial animals must be without defect to be accepted by the Lord.
Reiterates the prohibition against offering animals with defects, specifically mentioning blindness and lameness.
Forbids offering an ox or sheep with any defect, calling it an abomination to the Lord.
The prophet Malachi rebukes the people for bringing blind, lame, and sick animals as offerings, in violation of this command.
Malachi condemns those who offer injured animals and calls it a profaning of the Lord's name.
The Passover lamb was to be without defect, a fundamental principle for all offerings to the Lord.
Christ is described as a lamb without blemish or spot, fulfilling the requirement for perfect sacrifices.
Christ offered himself without defect to God, the ultimate fulfillment of the Old Testament sacrificial requirements.
